title: Silence in heaven (Revelation 8:1)
hookLine: the seventh seal opens, and heaven goes silent for half an hour

cards: Since the door opened in heaven, it has been loud. Lightning and thunder around the throne. Creatures that rest not day and night.
A new song. Horses at the gallop. A cry from under the altar.
A crowd from every nation shouting salvation. Then the Lamb opens the seventh seal, the last of the seven, and you'd expect the loudest moment of all. Instead, the whole book stops.
One verse: "And when he had opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven about the space of half an hour."

teach.b: First, the verse itself. It's short, and it doesn't explain. Even the length is loose: about half an hour.

No song, no thunder, no voice is mentioned. Second, what the silence might mean. Some hear awe, the hush of the prophets: "But the LORD is in his holy temple: let all the earth keep silence before him."
Others hear a held breath, a pause before the seven trumpets that come next. Revelation leaves both open. Third, what comes right after.

teach.h: INCENSE AND THE PRAYERS OF THE SAINTS.
teach.b: Seven angels are given seven trumpets, and then another angel stands at the altar with a golden censer and much incense, "that he should offer it with the prayers of all saints upon the golden altar which was before the throne."
And then: "the smoke of the incense, which came with the prayers of the saints, ascended up before God out of the angel's hand."
Some readers suggest heaven goes quiet so the prayers can be heard, perhaps even the cry from under the altar, how long. The text doesn't say so. But after the quiet, the prayers rise.
Fourth, the ordinary day. Heaven in this book is full of song, and it still has room for silence.
A psalm puts it plainly: "Be still, and know that I am God." Some churches keep a silence after a reading or before the prayers.
Some readers take from this that stillness belongs inside worship, not in the gaps around it.

how: Some Christian services include a time of silence after the readings or before prayers, and some Christians keep times of silent prayer or retreat, drawing on verses like Psalm 46:10 and Habakkuk 2:20.

games.why: "there was silence in heaven about the space of half an hour." and soon after, the prayers of the saints rise with the incense.

practice: Heaven kept about half an hour; let these few minutes be the start of yours, with your phone face down and no words to fill the quiet, not even good ones.

Let sounds come and go, a car, a fridge, your own breath, and let them pass like smoke rising. If you pray, let this be a prayer without words, rising like the incense; if not, just let the silence be what it is.
